question: Select the most appropriate option to fill In blank no. 2.
solution:
The correct answer is option 2.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Let's see the meaning of the sentence and the words given in the options.
 
 
• We landed we found a crowd of merchants and clients eager (2) ________ business with us. This line shows that the when they landed they come to know that the merchants were eagar
 
• Here, we need Infinitive to complete the meaning of the sentence.
 
• Do is the root form of the Main Verb
 
• To do is the To+ Infinitive.
 
• So the correct sentence will be "**To Do".**
 
 
 
• The complete sentence will be "**Wherever we landed we found a crowd of merchants and clients eager to do business with us. **

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__****

 
• ** ****Do is the main verb here**.

 
 
• "We" is the subject of the sentence and it is followed by the Main Verb **Found**
 
• According to the grammatical structure, we can not use only do.
 
• **So option 1 is the wrong answer**.
 
 
 
• "**Doing" **is a Present Participle form of Main Verb (Do)
 
 
• Present Participle form is preceded by helping verbs such as ""**am/is/are/was/were/have been/ has been/ had been/ shall be / will be / shall have been/ will have been"**
 
• In Present Continuous, Past Continuous, Future Continuous, Present perfect continuous, Past perfect continuous, Future perfect continuous tense.
 
• No such helping verb is used in the sentence
 
• **So option 3 is the wrong answer**.
 
 
 
• **To doing **is itself a wrong option.
 
 
• We use the to-infinitive after certain verbs (verbs followed by to-infinitive), particularly verbs of thinking and feeling:
 
• So use of "doing" after "to" is wrong.
 
• **So option 4 is the wrong answer.**
 
 
 
• **Use of Infinitives.**
 
 
• **​**An infinitive is a verbal, verb form or construction that plays the role of a different part of speech in a sentence.
 
• Although infinitives contain verbs, they cannot function as verbs.
 
• They do not convey a sense of tense on their own, and sentences containing them must include at least

 one finite main verb. 
 
• Infinitives are formed by placing **to in front of the base form of a verb**.
 
• They are negated by placing not in front of them.
